title: Persist durable per-attempt resource authority
description: Prerequisite for task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727. Current measurement at HEAD a42ae2f: @moe/scheduler ResourceRow reducers are pure; daemon has no durable current resource writer/reader or attempt-to-resource membership. ClaimSuccessors and ActivationLedgerRecord discard ResourceRow[], and recovery inventory is only a recovery-window snapshot, not live release authority. Deliverable: one focused daemon persistence/application module that binds the complete ResourceRow set to project/attempt/effect at claim or activation, records RELEASED/QUARANTINED transitions only through production @moe/scheduler reducers, and exposes a strict complete current reader. Consumer: task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727.
definitionOfDone: The production claim/activation path durably binds the complete ResourceRow membership to projectId, attemptRef and effect intent; a later resource cannot disappear merely because its row is undecodable or nonterminal.
State transitions are persisted only from accepted public @moe/scheduler resource-reducer results, preserving RELEASED versus QUARANTINED; caller row lists, refs or states never become authority.

A current per-attempt reader canonical-byte-checks and replays the bound set, returning every member exactly once; ABSENT, UNREADABLE, MALFORMED and AMBIGUOUS are distinct stable codes with exact layers and grant no terminal authority.

Real-Sqlite tests cover multiple resources, one undecodable row, one nonterminal row, replay/conflicting bytes, ordering, foreign-project binding, zero residue, and one accepted production-writer control; failure assertions pin code and layer.
Raw event/decision counts prove exact replay is idempotent and conflicting bytes do not overwrite the original set; a generated hostile sweep asserts a nonzero case count.
Completion names task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727 as consumer and records its exact reader edge; daemon typecheck/test execute separately with nonzero test-count output.
taskRails: Use public @moe/scheduler resource reducers after verifying manifest, lock importer and compiled bare-specifier dependency edge; do not reimplement their transitions.
Recovery inventory is not current scheduler resource authority and must not be repurposed. No caller list/ref/state gains authority.
Membership must be complete and bounded; missing, duplicate, undecodable or foreign-project rows are UNKNOWN/refused, never skipped.
Use real SqliteEventStore, TDD exact codes/layers, target <=250 lines per production source, and commit only explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description:
Land the contracts module apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-resource-authority-contracts.ts plus its one-line bridge `export * from "./attempt-resource-authority-contracts.ts";` (a new .ts module without its .js bridge is invisible to consumers while tsc and vitest both stay green).
Contents, names fixed here so later steps cannot drift:
- `ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_VERSION = "moe-attempt-resource-set/1"`, `ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_BOUND_EVENT_TYPE = "AttemptResourcesBound"`, `ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_TRANSITION_EVENT_TYPE = "AttemptResourceTransitioned"`, `ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_BIND_COMMAND_KIND = "work.attempt_resources_bind"`, `ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_APPLY_COMMAND_KIND = "work.attempt_resources_apply"`.
- `DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RESOURCE = "DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RESOURCE"` — this module's OWN layer. A refusal raised by the activation reader or by a scheduler reducer keeps ITS code and layer; only decisions made here are reported under this name.
- Frozen closed code list + type: ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_SET_REFUSED, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_SET_NOT_ACTIVE, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_MEMBER_DUPLICATE, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_BINDING_MISMATCH, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_PROJECT_MISMATCH, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_ABSENT, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_UNREADABLE, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_MALFORMED, ATTEMPT_RESOURCE_RECORD_AMBIGUOUS. ABSENT/UNREADABLE/MALFORMED/AMBIGUOUS stay four codes and are never folded: an empty stream, a store that threw, bytes that no longer re-encode and two bind events name four different repairs.
- Refused/answer outcome types. Refused carries `{ ok: false, authority: "NONE", code, refusedBy, upstreamCode: string | null }` — upstream preserved verbatim so a scheduler AUTHORITY_* refusal is never flattened into ours.
- `deriveAttemptResourceAggregateId(activationAggregateId)`: length-framed sha256, exactly as `deriveAttemptReleaseAggregateId` does it. It MUST NOT be the activation aggregate: that stream is read by a strict exactly-one-plus-ordered-tail reader and a foreign event type there makes the activation itself unreadable.
- Strict member/body decoders over own data properties only (exact key set; never spread a caller record).

Land the BIND writer in apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-resource-authority.ts plus its `export * from "./attempt-resource-authority.ts";` bridge. `bindAttemptResources(store, binding, rows)` where binding = { activationAggregateId, commandId, correlationId, principalId, projectId }.
Order is the contract:
1. Re-read the COMMITTED activation: `store.readEvents(binding.activationAggregateId)` in try/catch (throw -> ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE) then `readFoundationActivationHistory(aggregateId, events, binding.projectId)`. Not ok -> ACTIVATION_UNREADABLE. This is also the foreign-project fence on the write side: that reader's `tracedProject` refuses a project mismatch.
2. attemptRef = durable.attempt.attemptId, effectIntentRef = durable.effectIntent.intentId, projectId = binding.projectId — all from the DURABLE record, never from a caller-supplied claim.
3. Admit membership through the public reducer: `grantSuccessorCapacity(rows, null)`. Pass null deliberately — with a ref proof the reducer CLEARS quarantines to RELEASED, so a proof-carrying bind could launder a quarantined resource into a released one. Not ok -> SET_REFUSED, with `issues[0].code` preserved as upstreamCode and the SCHEDULER's layer as refusedBy.
4. Require `set.allActive === true` (a scheduler-computed field, not a daemon re-derivation) else SET_NOT_ACTIVE. Require unique resourceIds across `set.rows` else MEMBER_DUPLICATE — parseRows does NOT dedupe, so this is the daemon's own completeness check and it refuses rather than collapsing two rows into one.
5. Persist `set.rows` VERBATIM — the reducer's frozen rebuilt rows, never the caller's array. Body: recordVersion, projectId, attemptRef, effectIntentRef, memberCount, members[] (each row's exact 7 fields), truthClass "DAEMON_VERIFIED".
6. Canonical bytes via encodeFoundationPayload; not ok -> RECORD_MALFORMED.
7. Commit ONE event at expectedVersion 0 via `commitExpectedVersionDecision`, key `{ commandId: <commandId>:RESOURCES, principalId, projectId }`, eventId COPIED from `<durable.grant.grantId>:RESOURCES` so a second bind collides on store-wide event-id uniqueness instead of landing a row nobody can choose between. Throw or non-EFFECTS_COMMITTED -> COMMIT_UNAVAILABLE.
8. Answer by calling the reader — never from the value just written.
Green the step-2 tests.

Land the strict CURRENT reader `readAttemptResources(store, activationAggregateId, expectedProjectId)`. Keep it in attempt-resource-authority.ts if that file stays under 250 physical lines; if it would exceed the cap, split the reader into apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-resource-reader.ts plus its .js bridge (the cap is per production FILE, not per task).
Algorithm, fail-closed at every branch:
- `store.readEvents(deriveAttemptResourceAggregateId(...))` in try/catch -> RECORD_UNREADABLE on throw; zero events -> RECORD_ABSENT.
- Event 0 must be BOUND at aggregateSequence 1; a second BOUND anywhere -> RECORD_AMBIGUOUS; any event type outside the two this module writes -> RECORD_MALFORMED; a sequence hole or out-of-order aggregateSequence -> RECORD_MALFORMED.
- Per event: decode -> re-encode -> `sameBytes(again.bytes, event.payload)`; drift -> RECORD_MALFORMED. Canonical bytes need BOTH the digest and the re-encode; a digest alone does not prove the row still canonicalises.
- Body decode is strict and exact-keyed; recordVersion mismatch -> RECORD_MALFORMED; body projectId !== expectedProjectId -> PROJECT_MISMATCH; a transition whose attemptRef/effectIntentRef disagrees with the bind -> BINDING_MISMATCH.
- Replay in aggregateSequence order, folding member state by resourceId. A transition whose member id set differs from the bind's (adds or drops one) -> MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED. Never skip a member and never synthesise one: an unreadable member makes the whole record UNKNOWN, not a shorter list.
- Answer frozen: `{ ok: true, authority: "DURABLE_RESOURCE_SET", digest, projectId, attemptRef, effectIntentRef, members }` with every bound member present exactly once and `state` carried VERBATIM from the accepted reducer result. Do NOT re-declare ACQUISITION_STATES locally (step 1(d) measured it absent from the @moe/scheduler root) and do NOT classify terminality here — that is the consumer's derivation, and two definitions of the vocabulary would drift silently inside durable bytes.
- Every refused branch returns authority "NONE": a refusal grants no terminal authority.
Tests: ABSENT before any bind; UNREADABLE on a store that throws; MALFORMED on a planted drifted payload; AMBIGUOUS on two bind events; PROJECT_MISMATCH on a foreign expected project — each pinning code AND layer.

Land the TRANSITION applier `applyAttemptResourceReport(store, binding, report)`. It reads the durable current set through the step-5 reader (never a caller list), runs exactly ONE public @moe/scheduler reducer over those durable members, and persists the reducer's returned `AcquisitionSet.rows` verbatim:
- report.kind CONFIRM -> `adapterConfirm(members, report.resourceId, report.epoch)`
- report.kind FAIL -> `adapterFail(members, report.resourceId, report.epoch, report.disposition)`
- report.kind GRANT -> `grantSuccessorCapacity(members, report.proofRef)`
A reducer refusal is returned with its own code as upstreamCode and the scheduler layer as refusedBy, and writes NOTHING. Nothing here re-derives a state, re-implements a transition, or repairs a row: RELEASED versus QUARANTINED survives solely because the reducer's rows are what gets encoded. A caller-supplied state, ref or row list is never consulted — the report identifies WHICH resource and WHAT the adapter said, never what the set becomes.
Commit as the next event on the SAME aggregate with `expectedVersion` = current event count, so a concurrent apply collides instead of both landing, and command key `<commandId>:RESOURCES:<expectedVersion>`.
Tests, each pinning code and layer: adapterFail on a 3-member set with one non-fenceable sibling persists RELEASED for the failed row and QUARANTINED for the sibling, and the reader returns BOTH plus the untouched third — assert the persisted states against the reducer's OWN returned rows, not against hand-written string literals (a test with both operands hand-written is a tautology). A nonterminal member left ACTIVE is still returned and still carries no terminal authority. Ordering: two transitions on the same resourceId fold in aggregateSequence order and the later one wins — assert a reversed fold would give a DIFFERENT answer, so the ordering assertion is not vacuous.

Wire the PRODUCTION call site in apps/daemon/src/activation/activation-ingress.ts. Hoist the `assemble({...})` result into a local, call `commitStage(...)` with it, and when — and only when — the outcome is ok, call `bindAttemptResources(store, { activationAggregateId: deriveActivationAggregateId(record.effectIntent.aggregateId, record.effectIntent.idempotencyKey), commandId: request.commandId, correlationId: request.correlationId, principalId: request.principalId, projectId: request.projectId }, rows)` where `rows` is read ONCE from `request.payload["slot"]` into a local. The payload is JSON-decoded by `decodeBoundedJsonBytes`, so it holds no accessors and a second read cannot return a different array — the hostile-getter TOCTOU between the claim leg and the bind is structurally impossible here. Do NOT re-run the claim to obtain the rows and do NOT widen ClaimSuccessors.
ORDERING IS DELIBERATE AND MUST BE COMMENTED IN THE FILE: the bind runs AFTER the activation commit because the binder re-reads the committed activation for attemptRef, effect intent and project. A bind refusal must NOT be converted into an activation refusal — the activation is already durable and reporting it as refused would be a false claim about a committed decision — and it must NOT be reported as an accepted binding. The observable is the reader answering RECORD_ABSENT, which grants no terminal authority and blocks the consumer's release. Write that reasoning as a comment in the file, not only in the commit message.
The REPLAYED disposition binds too: a second identical activation replays the bind at the store and the event count stays 1.
Test — the accepted production-writer control: drive `runEffectActivateCommand` with a 3-row payload and assert the reader returns all three members bound to the durable attemptRef and effectIntentRef. Second test — the production-reachable refusal: a duplicate-resourceId payload passes the claim leg (parseRows does not dedupe and reserveProviderSlot only checks state), the activation still commits ok, and the reader returns ABSENT, proving the ingress neither fabricates a binding nor lies about the activation.

Idempotence, conflict and the hostile sweep — DoD item 5.
- RAW COUNTS, not return values: after one bind, capture `store.readEvents(resourceAggregate).length` and the command-decision row for the bind key. Bind again with byte-identical input: assert the event count is STILL 1, the decision replayed, and the reader's digest is unchanged.
- CONFLICTING BYTES: bind again under the SAME command key with a different member set. Assert it is refused, the event count is still 1, and the reader still returns the ORIGINAL three members — a conflicting write must not overwrite the bound set. Pin the exact code and which layer refused; the store's idempotency conflict is not this module's decision and keeps its own code as upstreamCode.
- GENERATED HOSTILE SWEEP over the bind and reader inputs: per member field emit mutations (missing key, extra key, wrong type, -0, NaN, negative epoch, empty resourceId, non-NFC text, `__proto__` key, accessor-bearing row, revoked-proxy row, duplicate id, zero-length member list). Assert `cases.length > 0` BEFORE asserting outcomes — a sweep that silently generates zero cases passes while testing nothing — and assert each case refuses with a code from the frozen list under layer DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RESOURCE or the scheduler's, never a throw. A crash is not a refusal.
- Close every store in a `finally` on every exit path; a held SQLite handle kills the vitest worker with an error that looks unrelated.

MUTATION DRILLS — prove the failure-path assertions are attached to the production surface, since a green suite cannot show this on its own. Run each drill, record the exact test name that reddened, then restore the file and confirm the restored bytes hash-match the original (git status alone is unreliable in this shared worktree).
1. In bindAttemptResources, change `grantSuccessorCapacity(rows, null)` to `grantSuccessorCapacity(rows, 'proof-ref')` — the quarantine-laundering drill. If nothing reddens, the no-proof property is unasserted; add the assertion.
2. Make the duplicate-resourceId check a no-op (return the set unchanged) — the MEMBER_DUPLICATE test must redden, and on that assertion, not merely on a count.
3. In the reader, drop the `sameBytes` re-encode check — the MALFORMED drift test must redden.
4. In the reader's fold, make it skip an undecodable member instead of refusing — a NAMED test must redden; a silently omitted member is the exact false-completeness this record exists to prevent.
5. In activation-ingress.ts, delete the `bindAttemptResources(...)` call — the accepted production-writer control must redden. This is the consumer-edge drill: it proves production IMPORTS the module, not merely that the module loads.
If a drill survives, do not rationalise it — either the assertion has detached from its subject or the mutation is equivalent. Say which, in the completion notes, with the evidence.

REGRESSION AND GATE. Adding a second durable commit inside `runEffectActivateCommand` touches every test that drives an activation, so run the whole daemon package, not just the new file.
Run exactly:
`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck; TC=$?; pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test; TT=$?; echo "TYPECHECK=$TC TEST=$TT"`
Both exit codes are captured separately — do not pipe (a piped run reports the pipe tail's code) and do not `&&`-chain (a red typecheck then hides the test count line). READ THE OUTPUT: the test leg must print a `Test Files ... passed` count line with a NONZERO count. `pnpm --filter` prints "No projects matched the filters" and exits 0 when the package does not resolve, so exit 0 with no count line is UNVERIFIED, not passing. @moe/daemon resolves to apps/daemon (verified in step 1).
Then attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline: record repo-wide failures at the merge-base, again at HEAD, and confirm the delta intersected with this task's owned paths is EMPTY. Report any foreign red verbatim with its exact failing lines and file paths; never hide it and never fabricate green. A red your own diff caused in a foreign file is NOT excused by that rule — it is exactly what the delta detects.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, then complete. Load the `adversarial-self-review` skill and read the diff as an attacker:
- Can a caller get its own row list, ref or state into durable bytes on ANY path? Trace every field of the persisted body back to either the durable activation record or the reducer's returned rows.
- Can two activations for different attempts derive the same resource aggregate id? If the same attempt is activated twice concurrently, does expectedVersion 0 plus the grant-derived event id make the second collide rather than append?
- Does any refusal path write bytes before refusing? A handler that wrote a row and then refused sails through a return-value assertion — every refusal test must also assert zero events.
- Is the reader's `state` genuinely the reducer's output, or could a planted event supply an arbitrary token? State the answer honestly in the completion notes rather than claiming a guarantee the code does not make.
- Confirm every production file is under 250 physical lines (split before 400) and that no probe, scratch or generated file remains in the diff — including the step-1 `_edge-probe.ts`.
COMPLETION MUST RECORD, per the epic's consumer-edge rail: task-6d40078159e84d92b3293d7b366cf727 is the named consumer, and its exact reader edge is `readAttemptResources(store, activationAggregateId, projectId)` from apps/daemon/src/work/attempt-resource-authority.js, returning `{ ok, authority, members[] }` with per-member `state` carried verbatim from the accepted scheduler reducer and RECORD_ABSENT/UNREADABLE/MALFORMED/AMBIGUOUS as the four distinct fail-closed codes under layer DAEMON_ATTEMPT_RESOURCE. Also record that `applyAttemptResourceReport` has no production caller at HEAD — no adapter-report ingress exists — so the bind arm carries this task's production edge and the applier's caller belongs to a later task. Stage and commit ONLY the owned paths by explicit pathspec; never `git add -A`.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
1) WIDEN ClaimSuccessors with a resources field so admitted rows travel claim->activation. REJECTED: it touches work-kernel.ts, work-claim.ts and index-surface.test.ts (which asserts `keyof ClaimSuccessors` exactly) — three hot shared files — and buys nothing here, because the activation payload is JSON-decoded by decodeBoundedJsonBytes, so `payload.slot.rows` holds no accessors and a second read cannot return a different array. The TOCTOU that would justify the widening is structurally impossible on this ingress.
2) BIND ON THE CLAIM PATH. REJECTED: attemptRef does not exist until activateEffect mints the attempt, and the DoD requires membership bound to attemptRef.
3) BIND AS A SECOND EVENT INSIDE THE ACTIVATION COMMIT (one atomic decision). REJECTED: readFoundationActivationHistory is a strict exactly-one-plus-ordered-tail reader over the activation aggregate; a foreign event type there makes the ACTIVATION itself unreadable. The sibling attempt-release module documents the same constraint and derives its own aggregate; we follow it.
4) BIND BEFORE THE ACTIVATION COMMIT, activation conditional on it. REJECTED: a failed activation commit would leave an orphan resource row, and the binder cannot re-read a durable activation that does not exist yet.
5) EXPORT ACQUISITION_STATES FROM THE @moe/scheduler ROOT so the reader can pin the vocabulary. REJECTED for this task: a value export moves that package's export-count test and packages/scheduler is under active graph-beta churn (task-2a2b1b48, re-scoped 77e8cb44). Raised in #architects as a cheap ride-along for whoever is already editing that index.
6) HAVE THE READER RE-VALIDATE ROWS THROUGH A REDUCER on every read. REJECTED: grantSuccessorCapacity refuses a QUARANTINED set without a proof, so read-side re-validation would make a legitimately quarantined member unreadable — precisely the member the consumer needs to see.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD 8557296 (the task description's a42ae2f is stale; the discard sites it names are unchanged).

GAP CONFIRMED PRESENT (checked in both directions): `grep -rn 'ResourceRow|adapterConfirm|adapterFail|grantSuccessorCapacity|reserveAll|AcquisitionSet' apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v .test.` returns exactly ONE hit — apps/daemon/src/recovery/durable-recovery-inventory-shape.ts:1, a TYPE-ONLY import feeding durableResourceObservation, i.e. the recovery-window snapshot the task rails forbid repurposing as current authority. There is no durable current resource writer or reader in the daemon.

DISCARD SITES: work-claim.ts:86-98 `claimSlot` passes `slot["rows"]` into reserveProviderSlot, which parses them, requires every row ACTIVE, and returns ONLY a ProviderSlotReservation — the rows die there. ClaimSuccessors (work-kernel.ts:149-155) has exactly 5 fields, none a row list. ActivationLedgerRecord (activation-ledger-contracts.ts:101-124) has no resources field.

DEPENDENCY EDGE, all three legs measured: apps/daemon/package.json declares `"@moe/scheduler": "workspace:*"`; pnpm-lock.yaml carries the importer entry for apps/daemon; and compiled bare-specifier VALUE imports already exist and typecheck at work-claim.ts:1-8 (reserveProviderSlot, reserveForAdmission) and activation-ingress.ts:3 (activateProviderSlot, activateReservation). Step 1 still runs the throwaway probe because the rail asks for it explicitly.

SCHEDULER ROOT SURFACE (packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:96-102 and 275-292): the resource entry points reachable through the bare specifier are activateProviderSlot, adapterConfirm, adapterFail, grantSuccessorCapacity, reserveAll, reserveProviderSlot, plus the types (ResourceRow, AcquisitionSet, AcquisitionState...). `parseRows`, `ACQUISITION_STATES` and `ACQUISITION_FAILURES` are NOT on the root — grep returns zero. That one fact drives two design choices: membership must be admitted through grantSuccessorCapacity (the only public reducer that accepts an arbitrary in-state row set and returns it), and the reader must carry `state` verbatim instead of re-declaring the enum.

WHY grantSuccessorCapacity(rows, null) IS THE ADMISSION and not a repurpose: it runs parseRows internally, so the persisted rows are scheduler-rebuilt frozen records and the caller's array never survives; it REFUSES when any row is QUARANTINED and no proof is given, which is exactly the fail-closed answer for binding an attempt to a resource nobody proved safe; and with nothing quarantined it returns `settled(rows,false)` carrying the scheduler's own `allActive`. Passing null rather than a proof ref is load-bearing — a ref would clear quarantines to RELEASED inside the bind.
